summary: Built 1924 as a 60-ft steel Aermotor lookout at Mizpah, Atlantic County, NJ; moved one mile and raised to 100 ft in 1959; listed on the NHLR in 2004.

facts.design: Steel Aermotor tower, originally 60 ft with 7'x7' metal cab; raised to 100 ft in 1959

events.note: Built 1924 near the old Mizpah Hotel; newspapers of June 1924 report it nearly erected
Moved one mile up the road to its present site (register only)
Raised from 60 ft to 100 ft at the time of the move (register only)

evidence.supports: built 1924 near old Mizpah Hotel; moved 1959 one mile up the road
evidence.quote: Originally constructed in 1924 near the old Mizpah Hotel, Mizpah Station Fire Tower was moved in 1959 one mile up the road to its present site.

evidence.supports: original 60 ft Aermotor with 7x7 metal cab, raised to 100 ft at the move
evidence.quote: The original 60’ Aermotor tower with 7’x7’ metal cab was raised to 100’ at this time.

evidence.supports: recently restored; key tower of the southern region of the Pinelands (undated)
evidence.quote: Recently restored, it is the key tower of the southern region of the Pinelands.

evidence.supports: administered by New Jersey Forest Fire Service
evidence.quote: Administered by New Jersey Forest Fire Service

evidence.supports: March 28, 1924 notice: fire warden arranged for a large steel tower at Mizpah
evidence.quote: Fire Warden Maurice F. Aaron has arranged for a large steel fire tower to be erected at Mizpah, larger than the McKee City tower

evidence.supports: notice: tower would help guards locate fires as soon as they start
evidence.quote: enable guards to locate fires accurately as soon as they start
Fire Warden Maurice Aaron reports the new steel fire tower at Mizpah nearly erected and expects it to be completed during to next week.

evidence.supports: height 100 ft (30 m), elevation 106 ft (32 m), Hamilton Township
evidence.quote: 570 23 - Mizpah Station 106 feet (32 m) 100 feet (30 m)

evidence.supports: Mizpah station is in Hamilton Township

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1924 newspaper notices place the tower at Mizpah; the register says the first tower stood near the old Mizpah Hotel and was moved in 1959. Consistent, but the 1959 move is documented only by the register.

sources.title: List of New Jersey Forest Fire Service fire towers

notes_for_editor: The 1959 move and the 'recently restored' claim rest on the undated NHLR page alone. No staffing, fire, or access sources found. The NJFFS fire-towers page at dep.nj.gov returned empty via fetch_text and WebFetch. Fact-check 2026-10-08: NHLR page confirms the agency, the March 15, 2004 registration, the 1924 build and the 1959 move; the 1924 notices are dated March 28 and June 22, 1924; the Wikipedia row lists Hamilton Township.
